newsitem.title: USA: 39 dead in apparent suicides outside San Diego.
newsitem.headline: 39 dead in apparent suicides outside San Diego.

text.p: Deputies found 39 young men dead at the scene of an apparent mass suicide in a luxury mansion on Wednesday, a San Diego Sheriff's Deputy said.
Capt. Alan Fulmer told reporters there was no blood or sign of trauma at the scene in Rancho Santa Fe, some 20 miles (32 km) north of San Diego.
He said the men, all 18 to 24 years old, were similarly dressed -- in dark pants and dark tennis shoes, although he did not describe their shirts.
There was no immediate comment on whether the men were members of a religious cult.
Sgt. Don Crist earlier said the department received a call in the afternoon about bodies at a house in the exclusive community of Rancho Santa Fe.
Deputies who went to the house found at least 10 bodies, Crist said. "They lost count at 10," he said.
Local TV station, KFMB, quoted a reporter at the scene as saying the bodies were in a "multimillion-dollar house" in Rancho Santa Fe.
The house, with a tennis court and swimming pool, and surrounded by horse ranches, had been rented by a group of people since October 1996, the reporter said, quoting neighbours.
The incident came after a cult suicide in Saint Casimir, Quebec last weekend.
Five members of a notorious doomsday cult died in a blazing house Saturday in an apparent ritual suicide pact, but spared three teenage children, Quebec police said.
And in 1994 and 1995, 69 members of the Solar Temple cult died in fires in Canada and Switzerland.
